issues.legal_issue: Materially inaccurate, untrue, or misleading factual statements in an application for special leave justify revoking leave granted on that application.
material_facts: The applicant’s special-leave petition asserted that the landlord had not relied on earlier rent defaults, although the plaint expressly relied on those defaults.
The petition also asserted that the applicant had made no default after a specified date, while omitting that a court deposit had been accepted without prejudice.
The respondent sought revocation of the special leave, and the Court found the statements materially inaccurate and untrue.
The applicant argued that counsel had not relied on the statements when leave was granted and that the statements had been copied from the earlier appeal.
issues.conclusion: The Court revoked the special leave and dismissed the appeal; it held that the arguments about what counsel urged at admission and where the statements originated did not answer the respondent’s request for revocation.
issues.legal_principle: When considering an application for special leave, the Court takes the petition’s factual statements and grounds at face value. Applicants must take care not to make material statements that are inaccurate, untrue, or misleading; doing so betrays the Court’s confidence and may justify revoking leave. The Court relied on no statutory provision or earlier case for this principle, and did not decide the underlying merits.

predicates.special_leave_proceeding: The matter before the Court is an appeal for which special leave was sought and granted.
predicates.petition_contains_material_falsehoods: The applicant made materially inaccurate, untrue, or misleading factual statements in the petition seeking special leave.
predicates.falsehoods_could_support_requested_leave: The false statements, if taken at face value, could assist the applicant in obtaining the requested leave.

issues.definition: When an appeal proceeds on special leave, material falsehoods in the leave petition that could support the request result in revocation of leave and dismissal of the appeal.
